# Implementation status — 2026-11-22

**Current milestone:** M0 offline starter plus independent audit reports (v0.2.0). **Tests:** see docs/proof/environment.json (regenerated by `npm run proof`). **Platform actually tested locally:** Node.js v24 on Windows 11. Hosted CI matrix (Ubuntu, Windows, macOS; Node 22/24) runs on GitHub Actions. Native IDE activation not executed.

## Implemented
- **v0.2.0:** independent audit (`intentsutra audit`, 11 checks AUD-01..11) writing sealed JSON, Markdown and HTML; `verify`; `--strict`; hardened CLI parsing; clean errors for hostile JSON; proof pack (TAP log, fuzzing, CLI transcripts); documents site; npm-ready package.
- Dependency-free Node.js CLI; JSON/Markdown requirement import; deterministic stable IDs; schema validation and source hashes.
- Ambiguity questions, reviewable Gherkin candidates and five-scenario fallback; no automatic stakeholder approval.
- Explicit local self-attested approval, revision-bound evidence, change history and stale-link detection.
- Evidence kinds: code/test/test-run/release/ticket/PR; imported pass/release claims not independently verified.
- Human attestation gate requiring current approval + code + imported passed test-run + imported release claim; final status remains evidence-linked, not completed.
- Traceability JSON/Markdown/HTML reports with escaping; local hash-chain audit and verification.
- Authenticated read-only 127.0.0.1 report API; project-local IDE instruction copier.
- 21 agent definitions, 26 portable SKILL.md, 8 workflows, 10 rules and 9 IDE instruction packs.

## Authored but not runtime-verified
Native agent/skill invocation in any of the nine IDEs, optional MCP/GitHub/ClickUp/Jira/OpenSpec/Spec Kit adapters, hosted CI matrix.

## Not implemented
Production multi-user server, verified SSO approvals, real code/test execution capture, interactive web dashboard, CI status import, deployed release proof, signed append-only audit, npm publication, public beta.

## Honest interpretation
An imported test-run file with outcome `passed` is still a **user-imported claim**. The product never asserts that code works or that a requirement is released based only on this data. Local reviewer names are self-attested and can be impersonated by someone with local write access.
